numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When `s` is set to any value greater than zero on large grids, `RectBivariateSpline` evaluates to NaN everywhere (i.e., `np.isnan(spl(x, y)).any()` is `True`). This happens irregularly: it may sometimes work but most of the time it does not. No warning or error is produced.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: With smoothing enabled (`s` non-zero), evaluating the spline should not produce NaN values for the test cases; the added test asserts `not np.isnan(z_spl).any()`.
trigger_conditions: Using `scipy.interpolate.RectBivariateSpline` with smoothing parameter `s` set to any value greater than zero (e.g., `s = 1`).
Using large 2D grids such as `nx=1000, ny=1700` (issue reproduction) or shapes `(350, 850)` / `(2000, 170)` (added tests).
Input data contains no NaNs (e.g., `np.random.randint(0, 100, ...)` or random integers cast to float).
The discrepancy may occur irregularly (sometimes works, most of the time it does not).
Problem occurs for data with dtype int as well as float.

input_output_examples.input: s=1; nx=1000, ny=1700; img=np.random.randint(0,100,size=(nx,ny)); x=np.arange(nx); y=np.arange(ny); spl=interpolate.RectBivariateSpline(x,y,img,s=s); compute np.isnan(spl(x,y)).any()

shape=(350, 850) or (2000, 170); rng=np.random.default_rng(1); x=np.arange(nx); y=np.arange(ny); z=rng.integers(0,100,(nx,ny)).astype(np.float64); spl=RectBivariateSpline(x,y,z,s=s); z_spl=spl(x,y); assert_(not np.isnan(z_spl).any()) with (s,atol,rtol) including (0,1e-12,1e-7), (1,7e-3,1e-4), (3,2e-2,1e-4)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: np.isnan(z_spl).any() is True (implied by the bug being fixed and the assertion in the added test)

oracle_clues: Issue oracle: the reproduction prints `np.isnan(spl(x, y)).any()`; the reported bug yields NaNs everywhere (`True`) without any warning/error message.
Test oracle: the added test computes `z_spl = spl(x, y)` and asserts `not np.isnan(z_spl).any()`.
Category/intent: PR title/description indicates a fix specifically for `NaN` output when smoothing large arrays in `interpolate.RectBivariateSpline`.

category_specific_evidence: RectBivariateSpline produces NaNs everywhere when smoothing parameter `s` is any value greater than zero (e.g., `s = 1`). Evidence shows this is tested with larger grid sizes: `nx, ny = 1000, 1700`, and checks `np.isnan(spl(x, y)).any()`.
The issue states the problem occurs on data with dtype int as well as float, and happens irregularly (sometimes works, most of the time it does not).

The PR notes two fix-related numerical/reliability conditions for large arrays: (1) recomputing knots when knots are maximised in a direction, and the tests check that output is non-NaN and that output is within a tolerance value; it also states that for larger `s`, the tolerance increases.

The PR/implementation exposes a `maxit` parameter (increasing maximal iterations for large arrays) by adding `integer optional :: maxit = 20` in `dfitpack.pyf`, and explains that for some values of `s` on large arrays, higher iterations are needed to converge to an acceptable solution.
The commit message indicates an added test for NaN output fix and a test for `s=2` case with increased maxit; it also notes skipping on 32-bit systems and decorating large tests as slow.
reproduction_risks: Repro may be irregular (“running the code sometimes work, but most of the time it does not”), so outcomes may vary run-to-run.

The PR indicates behavior depends on large-array settings and convergence iteration limits (`maxit`) for certain values of `s`, so changing array sizes or iteration budget may alter whether NaNs/tolerance failures occur.
For larger `s`, the expected correctness tolerance is higher, so using the wrong tolerance can misclassify a run as failing/succeeding.
